root_cause_summary: Deliverable 2 (display expansion) architecture: the data layer already fetches both windows — Claude parser (internal/usage/claude.go:99-138) fills PrimaryWindow (5H), SecondaryWindow (7-day) and TertiaryWindow (Opus); Codex parser (internal/usage/codex.go:166-186) fills Primary/Secondary from wham/usage. But the table renderer (internal/monitor/render_table.go:60-78) collapses everything to a single bar via usagePercent() (primary-window-only, alerts.go:110), discarding the weekly window, reset times, and any per-model data. Per-model usage (Fable / GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark) is not currently parsed: claude.go's claudeUsageResponse only decodes five_hour/seven_day/opus and drops unknown keys; codex.go decodes only rate_limit.{primary,secondary}_window. UsageInfo already has a ModelWindows map (internal/usage/usage.go:55) that is plumbed nowhere. Fix shape: (1) tolerantly capture per-model window keys into ModelWindows, (2) add one indented detail line per account under the existing row in the table renderer showing 5H/WK/model percentages with reset hints and strict graceful omission, (3) verify json/brief parity (JSON already embeds the full UsageInfo so ModelWindows flows through automatically; brief stays unchanged).

beads.title: Epic: expand caam monitor per-account display (5H + weekly + per-model usage)
beads.description_md:
Label: required_provider:any

## Goal
`caam monitor` (table format, default `--width 75`) currently shows ONE bar per account derived from the primary (5H) window only. Expand it so every account shows, in a genuinely pleasant, human-readable way:
- Claude: 5H window, weekly (7-day) window, and Fable model usage (if the API exposes it)
- Codex: 5H window, weekly window, and GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark usage 5H+weekly (if exposed)

## Hard constraints (user decisions, recorded 2026-07-03; user may veto)
- **Minimal lift**: extend the existing renderer in `internal/monitor/render_table.go`. NO redesign, NO new TUI, NO new dependencies.
- **D4 graceful omission**: per-model usage (Fable, GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark) may NOT be exposed by the usage endpoints (`GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`, `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage`). When a field is absent, it must be cleanly absent — no `--`, no `n/a`, no placeholder noise, no empty pipes.
- json/brief formats must stay coherent (see json-brief-parity bead).

## Target output (recommended layout — the exact spec for the render bead)
75-col table, innerWidth 73, keeping the existing account row untouched and adding ONE indented detail line under each account that has usage data:
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                            LIVE USAGE MONITOR                           |
|                          Last updated: 14:02:11                         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  CLAUDE                                                                 |
|  [OK] cabot@feta.fund       ########------------  42% | available       |
|       5H  42% (resets 1h12m) | WK  63% (resets 2d4h) | FABLE 18%        |
|  [WARN] saumil@feta.fund    ################----  81% | available       |
|       5H  81% (resets 44m) | WK  37% (resets 5d2h)                      |
|  CODEX                                                                  |
|  [OK] arthur@feta.fund      ######--------------  34% | available       |
|       5H  34% (resets 3h1m) | WK  54% (resets 4d18h) | SPARK 5H 22% WK 41%|
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
(If SPARK segment overflows innerWidth, drop reset hints from the detail line before dropping percentages — see render bead.)
Rejected alternatives: multi-column grid per account (redesign, violates minimal lift); second bar per window (vertical bloat, 2x rows already the budget); embedding WK in the status column (breaks existing `status` semantics at render_table.go:71-76).

## Architecture / task breakdown
1. `display-model-windows` — parse per-model window keys from both APIs into the existing (currently unused) `UsageInfo.ModelWindows` map (`internal/usage/usage.go:55`).
2. `display-detail-line` — render the detail line in `render_table.go`, incl. day-aware duration formatting.
3. `display-json-brief-parity` — verify JSON exposes new data (it embeds `*usage.UsageInfo` wholesale via `jsonProfile.Usage`, `internal/monitor/render.go:61,136`), keep brief unchanged, add tests.

## Dependency note
Depends on `fix-epic-external` (deliverable-1 monitor probe fix) only for END-TO-END verification: the probe currently returns 401/429 for stale vault tokens, so live output shows error rows instead of usage. Implementation and unit tests are NOT blocked (all render/parse tests use fixtures/mocks); merge coordinator may relax this edge if parallel execution is preferred.

## Acceptance (epic-level)
- `caam monitor --once` at default width 75 renders the block above cleanly for accounts with data; error rows (`usageUnavailable`, render_table.go:61-65) unchanged.
- `--no-emoji` (ShowEmoji=false) rendering stays aligned.
- Accounts whose API response lacks weekly or per-model data show only the segments that exist; an account with only a primary window shows `5H NN% (resets X)` and nothing else on the detail line; an account with no windows at all gets NO detail line.
- `go test ./internal/usage/... ./internal/monitor/...` passes; `go vet` clean.

beads.title: Parse per-model usage windows (Fable / GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark) into UsageInfo.ModelWindows
beads.description_md:
Label: required_provider:any

## Context
Repo: /data/projects/caam (Go CLI). `internal/usage/usage.go:55` defines `ModelWindows map[string]*UsageWindow` on `UsageInfo` — it is populated NOWHERE today. The Claude fetcher (`internal/usage/claude.go`) decodes only `five_hour`, `seven_day`, `opus` (struct `claudeUsageResponse`, lines 33-42); any per-model keys the API returns (e.g. a Fable-specific window) are silently dropped by `json.Decoder`. The Codex fetcher (`internal/usage/codex.go:36-52`) decodes only `plan_type`, `rate_limit.{primary_window,secondary_window}`, `credits`; any per-model breakdown is dropped.

Goal: capture per-model windows so the renderer can show `FABLE 18%` (Claude) and `SPARK 5H 22% WK 41%` (Codex). Decision D4: if the endpoint does not expose per-model data, `ModelWindows` simply stays nil — downstream must omit gracefully. Do NOT guess or fabricate schema: parse tolerantly.

## Spec
### Claude (`internal/usage/claude.go`)
1. Change response decoding to a two-pass tolerant approach: decode the body once into `map[string]json.RawMessage`, then unmarshal the known keys (`five_hour`, `seven_day`, `opus`) into `claudeWindow` exactly as today (keep the >1 percentage normalization at lines 99-138 intact).
2. For every OTHER top-level key whose value unmarshals cleanly into `claudeWindow` (has numeric `utilization`; `resets_at` optional), add it to `info.ModelWindows[key]` as a `*UsageWindow` with the same normalization (`util>1 => /100`), `UsedPercent: int(util*100)`, `ResetsAt: parseISO8601(...)`. Keys that fail to unmarshal as a window (e.g. strings, bools, plan metadata) are skipped silently. Also mirror composite keys of the form `five_hour_<model>` / `seven_day_<model>` into `ModelWindows` under their full key with `WindowDuration` set to 5h / 168h respectively.
3. Do NOT change error handling (401/403/other branches, lines 80-89) — deliverable-1 beads own that.

### Codex (`internal/usage/codex.go`)
1. Add optional fields to `codexUsageResponse` decoded tolerantly: capture `rate_limit` sibling objects and any top-level or `rate_limit`-nested map of per-model limits if present. Concretely: decode the raw body into a struct PLUS a `map[string]json.RawMessage` shadow of `rate_limit`; any key under `rate_limit` other than `primary_window`/`secondary_window` that unmarshals as `codexWindow` (fields `used_percent`, `reset_at`, `limit_window_seconds`, lines 48-52) goes into `info.ModelWindows[key]`. Same for a top-level `model_usage`/`models` object if present: for each model name, if its value contains `primary_window`/`secondary_window` shaped like `codexWindow`, store them as `ModelWindows["<model>/5h"]` and `ModelWindows["<model>/weekly"]`.
2. Conversion identical to lines 167-185 (`Utilization: used_percent/100`, `ResetsAt: time.Unix`, `WindowDuration` from seconds).

### Model-name matching helper (used by renderer bead)
Add to `internal/usage/usage.go`:
```go
// FindModelWindow returns the first ModelWindows entry whose key contains
// substr (case-insensitive), or nil. Optional suffix filter (e.g. "five_hour", "5h", "seven_day", "weekly") may be empty.
func (u *UsageInfo) FindModelWindow(substr, suffix string) *UsageWindow
```
Deterministic when multiple keys match: pick lexicographically smallest key. Returns nil on nil receiver/nil map.

## Acceptance criteria
- Existing tests in `internal/usage/usage_test.go` (850 lines) still pass unmodified.
- New table-driven tests: (a) Claude fixture with extra keys `{"five_hour":{...},"seven_day":{...},"opus":{...},"seven_day_fable":{"utilization":18,"resets_at":"2026-07-05T00:00:00Z"},"plan":"max"}` → ModelWindows has exactly `seven_day_fable` with UsedPercent 18, WindowDuration 168h; `plan` skipped; Primary/Secondary/Tertiary unchanged. (b) Claude fixture with NO extra keys → ModelWindows nil/empty. (c) Codex fixture with `rate_limit` containing an extra `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` window object → captured; fixture without → nil. (d) `FindModelWindow("fable","")`, `FindModelWindow("spark","weekly")`, nil-safety, case-insensitivity, tie-break.
- No behavior change for accounts/endpoints returning today's known schema (byte-identical UsageInfo apart from nil ModelWindows).
- Security: tests use fixtures only; no live API calls; never log token values.

beads.title: Render 5H/WK/per-model detail line under each account in monitor table
beads.description_md:
Label: required_provider:any

## Context
Repo: /data/projects/caam. `internal/monitor/render_table.go` renders one row per profile inside a bordered 75-col box (default `Width` 75 → `innerWidth` 73; floor 40, lines 15-26). Rows are built at lines 60-78: error rows via `usageUnavailable()` (`internal/monitor/alerts.go:73`), data rows as `"  %s%-20s %s %s | %s"` (indicator, name, 20-char bar from `progressBar()` render.go:183, percent, pool status/cooldown). `writeLine` (render_table.go:103) hard-truncates to innerWidth and pads — content can never break the box. `formatDuration` (render.go:198-214) formats up to hours (`"5h 3m"`), no day unit. Data source: `ProfileState.Usage *usage.UsageInfo` (state.go:22) with `PrimaryWindow` (5H), `SecondaryWindow` (weekly), `ModelWindows` (populated by bead display-model-windows), each `*UsageWindow{UsedPercent int, ResetsAt time.Time}` (usage.go:12-24).

## Spec
After writing the existing per-profile line (render_table.go:78), if the profile has a non-error usage (`usageUnavailable(p.Usage) == ""`) AND at least one of PrimaryWindow/SecondaryWindow/relevant model window is non-nil, write ONE additional detail line:

```
|       5H  42% (resets 1h12m) | WK  63% (resets 2d4h) | FABLE 18%        |
```

Rules:
1. **Segments**, joined with `" | "`, indented 7 spaces to sit under the profile name:
   - `5H {UsedPercent}%` + optional ` (resets {dur})` — from PrimaryWindow.
   - `WK {UsedPercent}%` + optional ` (resets {dur})` — from SecondaryWindow.
   - Claude profiles (`p.Provider == "claude"`): `FABLE {UsedPercent}%` from `p.Usage.FindModelWindow("fable", "")` (helper added by display-model-windows). If a weekly-vs-5H distinction exists (both `FindModelWindow("fable","five_hour")` and `("fable","seven_day")` non-nil), render `FABLE 5H n% WK m%`; if only one window, plain `FABLE n%`.
   - Codex profiles: `SPARK 5H n% WK m%` from `FindModelWindow("spark","5h")` / `("spark","weekly")` (also try substring `"codex-spark"`); if only one exists render just that one (`SPARK 5H n%` or `SPARK WK m%`).
2. **Graceful omission (decision D4)**: a nil window produces NO segment — no placeholder, no dangling `|`. If zero segments, no detail line at all. Reset hint omitted when `ResetsAt.IsZero()` or already past.
3. **Width discipline**: build the line with reset hints; if `len(line) > innerWidth`, rebuild WITHOUT reset hints (percent info always wins over reset hints). Never rely on writeLine truncation for the happy path at width 75; truncation remains the final safety net for width 40.
4. **Duration format**: add day support so weekly resets read `2d4h` not `52h`. Extend `formatDuration` (render.go:198) — or add `formatDurationCompact` if changing formatDuration breaks cooldown display tests (render_test.go) — with: `>= 24h` → `NdMh` (omit `Mh` when 0), `< 1h` → `Nm` (no seconds needed here). Reset hint uses `time.Until(w.ResetsAt)`.
5. **No redesign**: do not touch the header, borders, provider grouping (lines 49-53), error rows, or the primary row format. `ShowEmoji=false` must not change detail-line indentation (detail indent is constant, independent of indicator).

## Acceptance criteria
- Rendered example above reproduced by a unit test at Width 75 with a fabricated MonitorState (claude profile: 5H 42% reset in 1h12m, WK 63% reset in 2d4h, ModelWindows["seven_day_fable"]=18%; codex profile: 34%/54% + spark 5H 22% WK 41%). Assert exact detail-line strings and that every output line is exactly 75 chars.
- Omission cases tested: only PrimaryWindow → `5H 42% (resets 1h12m)` alone; nil Usage windows → no detail line; error row (`Usage.Error` set) → no detail line; codex with no spark windows → `5H ... | WK ...` only (matches today's live accounts).
- Width 40 renders without panic; lines are 40 chars (truncation acceptable there).
- `ShowEmoji=false` case tested for alignment.
- Existing tests in `internal/monitor/render_test.go` (181 lines) pass, updating only expectations that legitimately gained detail lines.
- `go vet ./...` clean; no new dependencies.

beads.title: JSON/brief format parity + regression tests for expanded monitor data
beads.description_md:
Label: required_provider:any

## Context
Repo: /data/projects/caam. `caam monitor` supports formats table/brief/json/alerts. JSON: `encodeJSONState` (`internal/monitor/render.go:111-152`) embeds the whole `*usage.UsageInfo` as `jsonProfile.Usage` (render.go:61), so new fields (`ModelWindows`, populated by bead display-model-windows) flow through automatically via the `model_windows` JSON tag (`internal/usage/usage.go:55`). Brief: `internal/monitor/render_brief.go` prints one worst-profile percent per provider, capped at 80 chars — per user constraint (minimal lift) it should NOT gain per-model data.

## Spec
1. **JSON**: no code change expected. Add a test in `internal/monitor/render_test.go` that renders a state whose UsageInfo has PrimaryWindow, SecondaryWindow, and `ModelWindows{"seven_day_fable": ...}` through `JSONRenderer{Pretty:false}` and asserts the output contains `"model_windows"` with the fable entry and both windows, and that a profile WITHOUT ModelWindows omits the key entirely (`omitempty` — verify tag, usage.go:55). If `omitempty` is missing on any newly-touched field, add it.
2. **Brief**: assert byte-identical output before/after the display change for a representative state (guards against accidental coupling; `usagePercent` at alerts.go:110 must remain primary-window-based).
3. **Alerts format**: no change; add one smoke assertion that AlertRenderer output for a profile with ModelWindows set is unchanged vs. without.
4. **CLI smoke**: extend or add a test (see `internal/monitor/monitor_test.go`, 179 lines, for state-construction patterns) covering `--format json --once`-equivalent rendering path if such a harness exists; otherwise renderer-level tests suffice.

## Acceptance criteria
- `go test ./internal/monitor/...` passes; new tests cover: model_windows present in JSON when set, absent when nil, brief unchanged, alerts unchanged.
- No schema-breaking rename of existing JSON keys (`usage_percent`, `usage`, `health`, `pool_status`, etc., render.go:57-67) — external consumers may parse them.
- No live API calls in tests; fixtures only.
